sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by stable lentiviral transduction (L1). K562 cells expressing FLAG-tagged constructs (including stalk-Flag) supported WEEV infection in a viral attachment/internalization assay, demonstrating that the FLAG insertion at S696–G697 does not abrogate the receptor function of the extracellular stalk (L5).
sites.rationale: All five ledger lines name the identical S696–G697 junction in the extracellular stalk of PCDH10. Python lookup confirms seq[695]='S' and seq[696]='G', matching the papers exactly. Position 696 lies within the extracellular span (19–724) and is 29 residues from the TM boundary (725), well above the 3-residue minimum. The stalk region (after EC6 domain, ~G690 onward) is a flexible linker with no known ligand-contact or disulfide residues at this position, consistent with tolerance of an 8-aa FLAG insert. Full-length human PCDH10 (NM_032961.3) with endogenous signal sequence and internal FLAG tag inserted between S696 and G697, synthesized and cloned into pSFFV-IRES-puromycin lentiviral vector for stable surface expression in mammalian cells (L1). Truncation constructs carrying the same S696–G697 FLAG junction (stalk-Flag, EC1-Flag, EC2-Flag) were expressed on K562 cells and tested for WEEV infection (L2, L5).

sources.claim: A codon-optimized H. sapiens (human) PCDH10 ( NM_032961.3 ) or P. montanus (sparrow) PCDH10 ( XM_039733439.1 ) with the endogenous signal sequence and internal Flag-tag inserted between residues S696 and G697 ( H. sapiens PCDH10) was synthesized and cloned into the pSFFV-IRES-puromycin lentiviral transfer vector by Twist Biosciences.

literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) converge on the single junction S696–G697 in the extracellular stalk. L1 is the primary anchor (full-length PCDH10, stable surface expression). L5 provides functional validation via WEEV infection assay on K562 cells. L2–L4 describe truncation constructs (stalk-Flag, EC1-Flag, EC2-Flag) that reuse the same junction but are not full-length membrane-anchored proteins; they corroborate the junction's tolerance but do not constitute independent sites. No other residue or loop is named in the ledger. The mature N-terminus (residue 19, after signal peptide cleavage at 18) is extracellular but no ledger line supports a tag there. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are reported in the ledger.
